articles.title: Airbus deal: Namal to be produced before Trial-at-Bar tomorrow
articles.text:
Parliamentarian Namal Rajapaksa, who is currently in remand custody over the controversial Airbus transaction, has been ordered to be produced before the Colombo Permanent High Court Trial-at-Bar tomorrow (28).
The order was issued by Colombo Chief Magistrate Asanga S. Bodaragama when the case was taken up today (27).
The Magistrate also directed that Rajapaksa remain in custody until his appearance before the Trial-at-Bar and ordered that a report on the proceedings be submitted to the Magistrate’s Court on October 30.
The development follows the filing of indictments against Rajapaksa and three other individuals before the Permanent High Court Trial-at-Bar over allegations of money laundering and accepting a Rs. 100 million bribe linked to the Airbus deal.
Earlier today, Deputy Solicitor General Janaka Bandara informed the Colombo Chief Magistrate’s Court that the indictments had been filed with the approval of the Chief Justice.
He informed the Court that the indictment contains 24 charges and lists 59 witnesses.
The Deputy Solicitor General also indicated that today’s proceedings were expected to mark the final occasion on which the matter would be heard before the Colombo Chief Magistrate’s Court, following its referral to the Permanent High Court Trial-at-Bar.
articles.summary: Parliamentarian Namal Rajapaksa, who is currently in remand custody over the controversial Airbus transaction, has been ordered to be produced before the Colombo Permanent High Court Trial-at-Bar tomorrow (28). The development follows the filing of indictments against Rajapaksa and three other individuals before the Permanent High Court Trial-at-Bar over allegations of money laundering and accepting a Rs. 100 million bribe linked to the Airbus deal.

articles.title: BASL calls for independent investigation into Homagama custodial death
articles.text:
The Bar Association of Sri Lanka (BASL) has expressed grave concern over the death of a 29-year-old suspect while in the custody of the Homagama Police, calling for an immediate, impartial and transparent investigation into the circumstances surrounding his death.
In a statement, the BASL identified the deceased as Ishara Harshakumara, a father of two from Kiriwaththuduwa, who had been arrested in connection with a drug-related investigation.
The Association said family members who visited the Homagama Police Station on October 25 had reported observing physical injuries on the suspect, which they believed indicated that he had been severely assaulted.
However, the BASL noted that the Police Spokesman had provided a different account, stating that the suspect had developed a sudden illness during an operation and died following admission to hospital.
Highlighting these conflicting accounts, the Association stressed the need for a credible and independent investigation to establish the circumstances surrounding the death.
The BASL emphasised that the State has a fundamental responsibility to protect the lives, health and physical safety of individuals in police custody.
It further stated that any allegation of custodial violence or ill-treatment must be treated seriously and that those responsible, if wrongdoing is established, must be held accountable under the law.
The Association noted that the Homagama Magistrate’s Court had ordered a post-mortem examination and that a preliminary inquiry had commenced under the direction of the Homagama Assistant Superintendent of Police.
However, it called on the Inspector General of Police and relevant authorities to ensure that all evidence is properly preserved and examined, with investigations conducted without interference or prejudice.
The BASL also stated that it would consider further action if necessary and keep its members and the public informed of developments.
articles.summary: The Bar Association of Sri Lanka (BASL) has expressed grave concern over the death of a 29-year-old suspect while in the custody of the Homagama Police, calling for an immediate, impartial and transparent investigation into the circumstances surrounding his death. Highlighting these conflicting accounts, the Association stressed the need for a credible and independent investigation to establish the circumstances surrounding the death.

articles.title: Brazilian leader Lula responds to President AKD, calls for stronger ties
articles.text:
Newly elected Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has expressed hope of strengthening bilateral trade and technical cooperation between Brazil and Sri Lanka, responding to a congratulatory message from President Anura Kumara Dissanayake following his election victory.
In a post on ‘X’ , Lula recalled his meeting with President Dissanayake in India in February this year and welcomed the opportunity to deepen relations between the two countries.
“My dear @anuradisanayake, it was a pleasure to meet with you in India in February of this year,” Lula stated.
Referring to his election victory, the Brazilian leader said the people of Brazil had demonstrated that democracy could be defended against disinformation and extremism.
“The Brazilian people showed that it is possible to defend democracy against disinformation and extremism. It was a great victory! I hope we can deepen technical cooperation and bilateral trade between our countries,” he added.
Earlier, President Dissanayake congratulated Lula on his election victory, describing the result as a defeat for corruption, division and political misinformation.
“Today, the people of Brazil did not just win an election; they defeated the forces of corruption, division and political lies,” President Dissanayake stated on X.
He further described Lula’s victory as historic, saying it demonstrated that people could not be misled by political dynasties and forces of the past.
“Many congratulations, companheiro, for leading the march of progress yet again!” President Dissanayake added.
articles.summary: Newly elected Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has expressed hope of strengthening bilateral trade and technical cooperation between Brazil and Sri Lanka, responding to a congratulatory message from President Anura Kumara Dissanayake following his election victory.

articles.title: Foreign Service Association funds water purification plant in Anuradhapura and Kattuwa Railway Station upgrade
articles.text:
The Sri Lanka Foreign Service Association (SLFSA) has handed over funds to the Sri Lanka Navy for the installation of a Reverse Osmosis (RO) water purification plant in Palagala, Anuradhapura, which is expected to provide safe drinking water to more than 1,750 people.
According to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Foreign Employment and Tourism, the cheque was handed over to Sri Lanka Navy Director General (Services) Rear Admiral H. I. A. Gunawardena by Foreign Minister Vijitha Herath and SLFSA members at a ceremony held at the Ministry on Monday (26).
The water purification plant, to be installed by the Sri Lanka Navy for the Thushara Funeral Aid Society in Palagala, is expected to benefit approximately 406 families.
The Ministry noted that Anuradhapura is among the districts most affected by Chronic Kidney Disease of unknown aetiology (CKDu), highlighting the importance of providing access to safe drinking water.
The project was funded through contributions from members of the Diplomatic Corps, Anjuman E Saifi (Sri Lanka) Trust Vice President Khuzaimah Jafferjee and CHEC Port City Colombo (Private) Limited.
The contributions had initially been made in support of the Annual Diplomatic Bazaar and Cultural Extravaganza, which could not be held as scheduled due to unforeseen circumstances.
Meanwhile, at the same ceremony, SLFSA President Anzul Jhan handed over a cheque worth Rs. 1 million to representatives of the Palagathurai Village Development Society for the modernisation of Kattuwa Railway Station in Negombo.
The funds, contributed by SLFSA members, will support a community-led initiative spearheaded by the Kattuwa Railway Family committee to improve facilities for local and foreign passengers.
The planned improvements include renovating sanitary facilities, repainting the station premises, providing drinking water and improving the station’s overall appearance.
The Palagathurai Village Development Society will oversee the implementation of the project, which forms part of the government’s broader initiative to upgrade railway infrastructure.
The ceremony was attended by Indonesian Ambassador to Sri Lanka and the Maldives Dewi Gustina Tobing, senior Navy officers, Health Ministry representatives, officials of the Foreign Ministry and members of the SLFSA.
articles.summary: The Sri Lanka Foreign Service Association (SLFSA) has handed over funds to the Sri Lanka Navy for the installation of a Reverse Osmosis (RO) water purification plant in Palagala, Anuradhapura, which is expected to provide safe drinking water to more than 1,750 people.

articles.title: Students achieve stunning Election victory in Serbia
articles.text:
A student-led political movement has secured a historic victory in Serbia’s parliamentary elections, ending more than a decade of political dominance by longtime leader Aleksandar Vučić and his Serbian Progressive Party (SNS).
According to preliminary results announced by Serbia’s Electoral Commission on October 26, the Student List won 52.71% of the vote, securing 140 seats in the 250-member parliament.
The alliance led by Vučić received 39.17% of the vote, securing 104 seats, according to the preliminary count.
Vučić conceded defeat following the October 25 election, acknowledging that the student-backed movement had won a parliamentary majority.
The result follows nearly two years of student-led demonstrations against alleged government corruption and authoritarianism.
The protests began after the collapse of a railway station canopy in Novi Sad in November 2024, which killed 16 people. The tragedy triggered widespread public anger and demands for accountability, eventually developing into a nationwide movement calling for political change.
Students organised demonstrations across Serbia, attracting support from university lecturers, civil society groups and ordinary citizens.
Following the election results, tens of thousands of people gathered in Belgrade and other cities to celebrate, waving flags, chanting slogans and welcoming the defeat of the ruling alliance.
Speaking on behalf of the student movement, Belgrade University professor Radomir Sajcic declared victory and said the movement would now focus on building the country’s future.
The student-backed electoral movement, which emerged from the protests, campaigned on tackling corruption, strengthening democratic institutions and improving education.
However, questions remain over who will lead the next government, as the movement has deliberately avoided establishing a single political leader.
Its candidates include academics, medical professionals, actors and farmers, reflecting the broad coalition that emerged from the protests.
The parliamentary victory gives the movement the opportunity to form a government, although the final election results and the formal process of establishing a new administration are still pending.
The election marks a major political turning point for Serbia, with a protest movement originating in universities now positioned to lead the Balkan nation.
articles.summary: A student-led political movement has secured a historic victory in Serbia’s parliamentary elections, ending more than a decade of political dominance by longtime leader Aleksandar Vučić and his Serbian Progressive Party (SNS). The election marks a major political turning point for Serbia, with a protest movement originating in universities now positioned to lead the Balkan nation.

articles.title: Maximum 2 overseas franchise leagues a year: SLC tightens rules
articles.text:
Sri Lanka Cricket (SLC) is set to introduce stricter regulations limiting national players to a maximum of three franchise cricket leagues per year, including the Lanka Premier League (LPL).
Speaking at a press conference in Colombo, Sri Lanka Cricket Transformation Committee member Sidath Wettimuny said the new regulations would be strictly enforced to ensure players prioritise their national commitments.
SLC had previously introduced similar restrictions on franchise league participation. However, the regulations were not consistently enforced, with several players participating in more tournaments than permitted.
Under the proposed measures, players will also be required to return to Sri Lanka at least 10 days before an international commitment, allowing sufficient time for preparation.
Wettimuny acknowledged that there had been instances where Sri Lankan players returned late from overseas franchise tournaments before joining the national team.
He noted that similar situations had also occurred recently and said the committee was determined to prevent such problems from recurring.
The committee also plans to strengthen the process of issuing No Objection Certificates (NOCs) for overseas franchise leagues, with players’ fitness levels becoming an important factor in granting permission.
The proposed regulations are aimed at improving player fitness, managing workloads and ensuring national team commitments take priority over franchise cricket.
articles.summary: Sri Lanka Cricket (SLC) is set to introduce stricter regulations limiting national players to a maximum of three franchise cricket leagues per year, including the Lanka Premier League (LPL). The committee also plans to strengthen the process of issuing No Objection Certificates (NOCs) for overseas franchise leagues, with players’ fitness levels becoming an important factor in granting permission.

articles.title: Lightning warning issued for all 25 districts; red alerts for two
articles.text:
The Department of Meteorology has issued red-level severe lightning warnings for the Ampara and Batticaloa districts, while amber-level advisories have been issued for the remaining 23 districts.
According to the Natural Hazards Early Warning Centre, thundershowers accompanied by severe lightning are likely at several places in the Ampara and Batticaloa districts.
The advisory, issued at 11.30 a.m. today (27), will remain valid until 11.30 p.m. tonight.
The department warned that temporary, localised strong winds may also occur during thundershowers and urged the public to take adequate precautions to minimise damage caused by lightning.
The public has been advised to seek shelter indoors, avoid standing under trees and stay away from open areas, including paddy fields, tea plantations and open water bodies during thunderstorms.
People have also been advised to avoid using wired telephones, connected electrical appliances and open vehicles such as bicycles, tractors and boats.
The department further urged the public to remain cautious of fallen trees and power lines and to contact local disaster management authorities in the event of an emergency.

articles.title: Sri Lanka’s first woman Permanent Representative presents credentials to African Union
articles.text:
Sri Lanka’s Ambassador to the African Union (AU), Nirmala Paranavitana, has presented her Letters of Credence to African Union Commission Chairperson Mahmoud Ali Youssouf, becoming the first Sri Lankan woman to serve as the country’s Permanent Representative to the AU.
According to the Sri Lankan Embassy in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, the presentation was followed by discussions on strengthening relations between Sri Lanka and the African Union through enhanced South–South cooperation.
During the meeting, Ambassador Paranavitana proposed establishing a comprehensive AU–Sri Lanka Partnership Framework, supported by a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to identify priority areas and facilitate practical cooperation programmes.
The AU Commission Chairperson welcomed the proposal and expressed interest in pursuing an MoU and identifying opportunities for joint programmes and institutional partnerships.
The discussions focused on potential cooperation in agriculture and food security, youth empowerment, digitalisation, healthcare, technical and vocational education, climate resilience, water resource management and the Blue Economy.
Opportunities for technology transfer, entrepreneurship, investment, knowledge exchange and capacity-building were also explored.
Ambassador Paranavitana highlighted Sri Lanka’s willingness to share its expertise in agriculture, technology, water resource management and post-conflict reconciliation.
She also expressed interest in promoting agricultural research partnerships, digital innovation, youth entrepreneurship and stronger regional value chains between South Asian and African institutions.
Both sides reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening institutional ties and developing practical initiatives aligned with Africa’s development priorities and the African Union’s Agenda 2063.
Ambassador Paranavitana is a diplomat and scholar specialising in international law, security studies and transitional justice.
She was selected as a United Nations Law Fellow at The Hague Academy of International Law in 2024 and has previously served in New York, New Delhi, Myanmar, Tokyo and Sweden.
She holds an undergraduate degree from the University of Delhi and an MPhil from the Australian National University.
articles.summary: Sri Lanka’s Ambassador to the African Union (AU), Nirmala Paranavitana, has presented her Letters of Credence to African Union Commission Chairperson Mahmoud Ali Youssouf, becoming the first Sri Lankan woman to serve as the country’s Permanent Representative to the AU.

articles.title: Is Your Home’s Electrical System Safe? KEVILTON’s ‘Adhi Arakshawe Mehewara’ Strengthens Its Commitment to Home Safety
articles.text:
Home electrical safety is something many people tend to overlook until an electrical fault or accident occurs. However, identifying potential hazards early and taking the necessary precautions can help prevent serious electrical accidents. Recognising the importance of this, KEVILTON’s ‘Adhi Arakshawe Mehewara’ initiative continues to make a meaningful contribution to household safety by raising awareness and helping families create safer living environments.
Going beyond conventional business objectives, the initiative reflects KEVILTON’s commitment to making a positive difference in people’s lives. At its heart is a simple yet important belief: a safe home provides families with greater peace of mind.
A Humanitarian Initiative Supporting Families Affected by Cyclone Ditwah
KEVILTON launched the ‘Adhi Arakshawe Mehewara’ initiative to support families affected by property damage caused by Cyclone Ditwah in the previous year, as they worked to rebuild their lives.
Rebuilding a home after a natural disaster involves more than restoring walls and roofs. It also means ensuring that the home is safe for the people who live in it. Among the essential considerations in this process is the safety of the household electrical system, which can pose significant risks if faults go undetected.
Recognising this need, KEVILTON introduced the initiative with a focus on identifying potential electrical hazards before they lead to accidents. Rather than responding only after an incident occurs, the programme emphasises the importance of prevention, awareness and proactive safety measures.
Electrical Safety Inspections in Nittambuwa
Continuing this humanitarian effort, another phase of the ‘Adhi Arakshawe Mehewara’ initiative was carried out on 24 August 2026, focusing on houses in the Nittambuwa area.
The programme involved preliminary inspections of the electrical systems in these homes, with the aim of identifying existing issues and providing the necessary guidance to help prevent electrical accidents.
During the initiative, the electrical systems were examined to identify potential problems, while residents were given safety awareness guidance on preventing electrical hazards before they result in serious incidents.
Such inspections are important because electrical faults are not always visible during everyday use. Even when lights, switches and electrical appliances appear to function normally, this does not necessarily mean that the entire electrical system is safe.
By identifying potential problems and raising awareness of electrical safety, the programme highlights the importance of taking preventive action to protect households and their occupants.
Why Electrical Safety Must Be a Priority
A home is a place where families come together to live, relax and create lasting memories. Ensuring that it remains a safe environment is essential, and electrical safety is a key part of that responsibility.
Ignoring electrical faults can expose households to unnecessary risks. Regular inspections by qualified electricians, prompt attention to electrical problems and greater awareness of safe electrical practices can all help reduce potential hazards.
Taking preventive action before an accident occurs is far better than dealing with its consequences afterwards. This principle lies at the heart of KEVILTON’s ‘Adhi Arakshawe Mehewara’ initiative.
By focusing on early identification, safety awareness and prevention, the programme reinforces an important message: protecting a home means protecting the people who live in it.
A Continued Commitment to Safer Homes
KEVILTON’s ‘Adhi Arakshawe Mehewara’ is more than an electrical inspection programme. It represents a humanitarian commitment to the safety, well-being and peace of mind of families.
Launched to support communities affected by Cyclone Ditwah, the initiative continues to demonstrate the importance of looking beyond immediate recovery and addressing the safety needs of families as they rebuild their lives.
A safe home is defined not only by its walls and roof, but also by the security and well-being of the people within it. Paying attention to electrical safety, identifying potential hazards early and taking the appropriate preventive measures are essential steps towards creating a safer living environment for every family.
Through its ‘Adhi Arakshawe Mehewara’ initiative, KEVILTON continues to champion a proactive approach to home electrical safety, reaffirming its commitment to helping families enjoy safer homes and greater peace of mind.

Through its ‘Adhi Arakshawe Mehewara’ initiative, KEVILTON continues to champion a proactive approach to home electrical safety, reaffirming its commitment to helping families enjoy safer homes and greater peace of mind.

articles.title: Naadagama Melbourne: An Eight-Year Sri Lankan Musical Journey Reaches a Major International Stage
articles.text:
With a reported event budget of LKR 200 million, Naadagama Melbourne is being presented by its organisers as one of the largest Sri Lankan concert productions ever staged overseas. More than 5,000 tickets have already been sold for the October 31 concert, marking a significant milestone for a musical concept that began eight years ago with just 150 people.
The concert will take place at Melbourne’s iconic Sidney Myer Music Bowl, a celebrated Australian outdoor venue that has hosted internationally renowned acts including ABBA, AC/DC, Paul McCartney and Metallica. Bringing Naadagama to this stage represents an important opportunity to showcase Sri Lankan music within an internationally recognised concert setting.
Hosted by Manuranga Wijesekara, the event will feature Methun SK, Ridma Weerawardena, Dinesh Gamage, Dhanith Sri, Kanchana Anuradhi and Supun Perera, under the musical direction of Eshan Denipitiya.
According to the organisers, musicians from the Melbourne Symphony Orchestra will also join the performance. Established in 1906, the MSO is Australia’s oldest professional orchestra and a prominent institution in the country’s cultural life. The participation of its musicians will add a significant international dimension to Naadagama’s musical arrangements.
More than 35 artists and technical professionals are travelling from Sri Lanka, joining overseas musicians and production personnel for an ambitious production combining musical performance, sound, lighting and stage presentation.
The scale of the Melbourne event reflects the growth of Naadagama itself. Over eight years, the show has developed around the same core artist lineup, building a recognisable identity and a loyal audience.
From its first gathering of 150 people, Naadagama has grown to attract audiences exceeding 12,000 at a single show. According to its organisers, cumulative attendance has surpassed 80,000 over the years, including 40,000 within the past two years alone.
That continuity has helped establish Naadagama as a valuable Sri Lankan entertainment property, with an audience connection that extends beyond any individual concert.
Its influence also lies in the experience it helped popularise: taking the intimacy and attentive listening associated with an indoor musical performance into an outdoor setting. Audiences gather to sing, listen and connect with the artists, making that shared atmosphere a central part of the show’s identity.
Its organisers see Naadagama as an influential part of the wider growth of similar outdoor musical experiences in Sri Lanka. The Melbourne production takes that concept further, bringing its established format to an international venue while introducing a new way for audiences to participate.
For the first time, Naadagama will be presented as a hybrid experience, connecting concertgoers in Melbourne with online viewers around the world and an audience gathering in Colombo.
Through the SLVLOG Events Couch Pass, fans in Sri Lanka and overseas will be able to watch the Melbourne concert live, extending access to those unable to attend in person.
A special Naadagama Watch Party will also take place at City of Dreams in Colombo, allowing fans to share the live screening together. Following the Melbourne broadcast, guests will enjoy a live performance of Handiya Pocket Edition, bringing two musical experiences to one venue.
With its LKR 200 million investment, international setting, travelling production team and collaboration between Sri Lankan and Australian musicians, Naadagama Melbourne represents a significant step in the development of a Sri Lankan concert brand for audiences across borders.

articles.title: Substandard medicine case: TISL welcomes SC action over non-payment of Rs. 275M
articles.text:
Transparency International Sri Lanka (TISL) has emphasised the importance of compliance with judicial orders, following its contempt of court application against former Health Minister Keheliya Rambukwella and four former senior health officials over their failure to make payments totalling Rs. 275 million to the State.
In a statement issued following yesterday’s (26) Supreme Court proceedings, TISL said it had filed the contempt application on October 12, alleging wilful disobedience of the Court’s earlier judgment in the medical procurement case.
The proceedings stem from a Supreme Court judgment delivered on March 27, 2026, which found that the five respondents had violated the fundamental right to equal protection of the law guaranteed under Article 12(1) of the Constitution.
The Court had ordered Rambukwella to pay Rs. 75 million to the State, while the other four respondents were each directed to pay Rs. 50 million.
According to TISL, former National Medicines Regulatory Authority (NMRA) Chairman Prof. S. D. Jayaratne informed the Court yesterday that he had settled his payment of Rs. 50 million on October 22, following the filing of the contempt application.
Meanwhile, Rambukwella had paid Rs. 20 million on October 23 and undertook to settle the remaining Rs. 55 million within two weeks.
Former Health Ministry Secretary S. J. S. Chandraguptha undertook to pay Rs. 5 million within a week and the remaining Rs. 45 million within three months.
Former NMRA Chief Executive Officer Dr. Vijith Gunasekara agreed to pay Rs. 20 million within two weeks and the remaining Rs. 30 million within three months.
Former Medical Supplies Division Director Dr. A. Thusitha Sudharshana undertook to pay approximately Rs. 2 million from his savings within the week and settle the remaining Rs. 48 million within three months.
The Supreme Court directed the four respondents to settle their outstanding payments within three months, imposed travel bans and ordered their release on bail subject to a cash bond of Rs. 50 million each and two sureties.
TISL stressed that compliance with judicial orders is fundamental to the rule of law and constitutional accountability, adding that such compliance should not depend on petitioners initiating further court proceedings.
The organisation further warned that corruption carries long-term legal consequences and reputational damage, while reaffirming its commitment to monitoring public officials and ensuring accountability.
The case is scheduled to be taken up again on February 15, 2027.
articles.summary: Transparency International Sri Lanka (TISL) has emphasised the importance of compliance with judicial orders, following its contempt of court application against former Health Minister Keheliya Rambukwella and four former senior health officials over their failure to make payments totalling Rs. 275 million to the State.

articles.title: Kawanthissa’s death must be a lesson to end elephant killings in Sri Lanka: Sajith
articles.text:
Opposition Leader Sajith Premadasa has called for stronger measures to protect Sri Lanka’s elephant population, stating that the death of the tusker Kawanthissa must serve as a lesson to end the longstanding culture of elephant killings in the country.
Addressing the Parliamentary Forum on Climate Change, Premadasa said Kawanthissa’s death should be recognised as a killing, highlighting the need for effective solutions to prevent similar incidents in the future.
He emphasised that elephants and tuskers must be recognised as part of Sri Lanka’s national and cultural heritage and protected through a dedicated conservation programme.
The Opposition Leader proposed introducing a comprehensive conservation strategy specifically focused on elephants, alongside a national land-use plan and a people-centred environmental protection programme.
Highlighting the limited human and physical resources available to the Department of Wildlife Conservation, Premadasa called for greater state support to strengthen elephant conservation efforts.
He also raised concerns over the declining number of large-tusked elephants in Sri Lanka, calling for further investigations into the issue.
Premadasa proposed establishing a dedicated hotline to report sick elephants and tuskers, while urging the Department of Wildlife Conservation and organisations involved in elephant welfare to work together.
He further stated that the Parliamentary Forum on Climate Change was prepared to provide several multiparameter monitors required by veterinarians treating elephants.
The Opposition Leader also stressed the importance of involving civil society organisations and environmental activists in conservation efforts to prevent further elephant killings.
Meanwhile, addressing broader environmental concerns, Premadasa called for increased public awareness of the effects of El Niño and La Niña conditions, particularly at the grassroots level.
He said awareness programmes should reach communities across all Grama Niladhari divisions to improve public understanding of climate-related risks and environmental conservation.
Premadasa and Professor L. M. Abeywickrama serve as Co-Chairpersons of the Parliamentary Forum on Climate Change.
articles.summary: Opposition Leader Sajith Premadasa has called for stronger measures to protect Sri Lanka’s elephant population, stating that the death of the tusker Kawanthissa must serve as a lesson to end the longstanding culture of elephant killings in the country.

articles.title: Sri Lanka must embrace technology and new global order or risk becoming insignificant: Ranil
articles.text:
Former President Ranil Wickremesinghe has warned that Sri Lanka must undergo rapid economic and technological transformation to remain relevant in the emerging global order, cautioning that failure to adapt could leave the country increasingly insignificant on the international stage.
Addressing the 50th webinar of ICC Sri Lanka on Monday (26), Wickremesinghe said Sri Lanka must develop a strong, competitive economy through technology-oriented modernisation while positioning itself as a maritime logistics hub in the Indian Ocean.
“We in Sri Lanka must adapt to these changes, or we will be swallowed up by bigger fish. We need economic and social transformation based on technology-oriented modernisation,” he said.
The former President outlined several priorities for Sri Lanka, including closer economic cooperation with India, stronger relations with Bay of Bengal countries and Southeast Asia, and eventual regional economic integration.
He also called for Sri Lanka to join BRICS, strengthen relations with the United States, China, Russia and Japan, and adopt a more transactional approach to international relations.
Wickremesinghe further proposed reviewing the effectiveness of the Indian Ocean Rim Association (IORA) and BIMSTEC, accelerating the Colombo Security Conclave and developing a technologically advanced navy equipped with small and medium-sized vessels.
Highlighting the strategic importance of the Indian Ocean, he said Sri Lanka must safeguard its economic interests, particularly the continued operation of the Suez Canal and the Gulf, which he described as the country’s two economic lifelines.
Referring to the growing influence of artificial intelligence and emerging technologies, Wickremesinghe said technological capabilities were increasingly becoming a defining factor of national sovereignty and global power.
He noted that the United States and China were emerging as dominant powers in artificial intelligence and computing, while other countries, including India, Japan and several European nations, were advancing their technological capabilities.
The former President also highlighted the economic potential of the Bay of Bengal and the importance of protecting undersea communication cables and strengthening maritime security.
Warning against inaction, Wickremesinghe said Sri Lanka could not afford to remain outside the changing geopolitical landscape.
“Either we go this way, or we fade into insignificance, like one of the small Pacific islands,” he cautioned.
Full statement :
It is my privilege to be here at the 50th webinar of ICC Sri Lanka.
Addressing the NDTV World Summit, Prime Minister Narendra Modi described the present as a world between orders: the ending of one and the start of another. It is worth watching on YouTube. He highlighted the weaponisation of finance, trade, technology and shipping as part of today’s new geopolitics. The post-World War II institutions are unable to intervene because they have not adapted to the changing world order. The Prime Minister quoted Chanakya on the need to prevent Matsya Nyaya, the law of the fishes, where the strong swallow the weak.
The existing global order, which had its roots in 19th-century Europe, is being replaced by a new 21st-century order. That order is shaped by newly emerging forces, and by the newest of them all: technological advancement.
The Goldman Sachs report on the Generative World Order states that AI and data ownership, combined with dollar-dominated global financial markets, form the basis of U.S. dominance. China, the other AI superpower, is working with BRICS members to find an alternative through de-dollarisation. What we are witnessing today is a duopoly of AI and computing superpowers. China and America have also taken the lead in other technologies such as space, ocean and automation. There are also powers such as India, the UK, France, Germany, Israel, Japan and South Korea developing their own technology. So we have to remember that sovereignty today implies technology.
Where are we in Sri Lanka? Institut Montaigne calls this the end of the nation state. I think it is more a transformation. We are witnessing the decline of the geopolitics of Western-led alliances and the beginning of transactional geopolitics between the leading powers. According to the Oxford Institute for New Thinking, global governance will increasingly depend on pivotal power coalitions operating within a broader polycentric system.
We in Sri Lanka must adapt to these changes, or we will be swallowed up by bigger fish. We need economic and social transformation based on technology-oriented modernisation. I will say that again: we need economic and social transformation based on technology-oriented modernisation.
The Indian Ocean
The Indian Ocean will be one of the centres of the new global order, together with the emerging economic powers of Asia and Africa. It will strengthen its position as the main shipping artery connecting East and West, and its undersea resources are immense and available for exploration.
With the U.S.–Iran war, we are also witnessing the decline of the Indian Ocean as a zone of peace, of its freedom of navigation, and of U.S. power in West Asia. New power centres are emerging. In West Asia, Iran dominates on one side. On the other is the Mecca Pact of Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, Egypt and Turkey. Israel remains another player. Sri Lanka’s interest is in ensuring that its two economic lifelines, the Suez Canal and the Gulf, remain fully operational.
Second, we must not ignore the potential of the Bay of Bengal as an economic region. India, the dominant power in the region, ranks among the top three economies by GDP. Indonesia, expected to have the fourth or fifth largest GDP in the world by 2050, is extending its influence. It recently ordered new submarines from Italy and took over the aircraft carrier Garibaldi. Bangladesh will also emerge as an economic power. Southeast Asian economies and China are moving towards closer economic cooperation through western China. This is producing the Chengdu–Chongqing corridor extending to Myanmar and Bangladesh, which will give China a second point of access to the Indian Ocean, this time in the Bay of Bengal.
Third, we have an economic region at our doorstep: a market of 600 million people, excluding India.
Finally, there is the emergence of new technologies: the space–ocean–telemetry nexus. This includes orbital and maritime awareness satellites, guided hypersonic corridors, unmanned underwater vehicles and drones, which will play a major role in the security of the Indian Ocean. Protecting the undersea cables in our region is also a priority.
This new world order is already taking shape. We will see a trilateral meeting of the U.S., Russia and China in China. Whatever the outcome, these meetings will continue. This year alone, there will be four meetings between the Presidents of the United States and China.
What Sri Lanka must do
We in Sri Lanka must prepare for the new global order. The main requirements are:
Rapid technological modernisation, resulting in a strong, competitive economy. If we do not do this, we will have no place in the new world order.
Make Sri Lanka a maritime logistics centre.
Build closer economic cooperation with India.
Strengthen relations with the Bay of Bengal countries and Southeast Asia, leading eventually to regional integration.
Join BRICS.
Strengthen relations with the three major powers, the U.S., China and Russia, as well as Japan.
Engage in transactional geopolitics. There is no other way. We cannot sit it out.
Review the effectiveness of IORA and BIMSTEC. Both organisations need fundamental changes if we are to continue in them.
Accelerate the work of the Colombo Security Conclave. This will be important for the Indian Ocean now and in the future.
Build a technologically advanced navy with small and medium-sized ships.
This is what we must do to survive in a new global order where technology plays a central role and trade remains important. Either we go this way, or we fade into insignificance, like one of the small Pacific islands.
Thank you.

Former President Ranil Wickremesinghe has warned that Sri Lanka must undergo rapid economic and technological transformation to remain relevant in the emerging global order, cautioning that failure to adapt could leave the country increasingly insignificant on the international stage. We in Sri Lanka must prepare for the new global order.

articles.title: ‘Maxxing’ is Dictionary.com’s word of the year
articles.text:
From AI chatbots to lifestyle trends, the concept of optimizing one’s life came sharply into focus in 2026. That’s why Dictionary.com picked “maxxing,” a reflection of our increasingly online society, as its latest Word of the Year.
“Maxxing (sometimes -maxxing) is short for ‘maximizing,'” says Dictionary.com. “This trendy term can be used on its own or added to the end of any word to convey you’re doing something to the fullest or optimizing it as much as possible.”
The word was chosen following an analysis of search data, social media trends and news stories “to capture a society that’s deeply online and focused on optimization in all forms,” Dictionary.com says.
“Maxxing” rose through the cultural lexicons of Gen Z and Gen Alpha quickly, and now works as a noun, verb, adjective and adverb all at once. Leveling up your workout routine? “Gymmaxxing.” Your personal care practices? “Healthmaxxing,” an umbrella term that covers numerous subgenres, including “proteinmaxxing” and “fibermaxxing.”
“Maxxing really stood out this year because not only was it everywhere, in all types of articles, but it crossed a lot of different domains,” said Steve Johnson, the director of lexicography for Dictionary Media Group, which runs Dictionary.com .
At work, people talked about “tokenmaxxing,” meaning leaning ever harder on AI. In wellness circles, there was “sleepmaxxing.” Even leisure received the “maxxing” treatment, with “cozymaxxing,” as did politics, when the federal government used “homelandmaxxing” in some of its messaging.
“That’s not something that we often get with a lot of slang terms,” Johnson told CBS News.
How Dictionary.com picks a Word of the Year
Johnson keeps a running list of words to watch throughout the year, some of which have been rolled over from years prior and tracked for growing usage. To choose an annual winner, Dictionary’s lexicographers look at how often a word appears in news articles, on social media and in online searches. They also weigh a word’s cultural significance during selection.
“We not only look at the data behind the word usage, but we also are really looking to see what’s capturing something distinctive that describes the year,” Johnson said.
The latest word choice marks a turn from last year’s winner, “67,” a term that, despite its virality, left many bewildered over its meaning. “Maxxing” has had the opposite effect, Johnson said.
“‘Maxxing’ is so accessible,” he said. “People do understand it because it’s tied to something that people instrinsically get.”
What is “maxxing”?
The word itself isn’t new. “Maxing out” a credit card, or 100 miles an hour on the highway, are well-established uses that go back decades. But the newer, optimization-focused definition comes from game theory, Johnson said. In the 1940s, academics used “mini-max” to describe a strategy for minimizing their maximum possible losses, an idea that later moved into contemporary games like Dungeons & Dragons. In that context, “min-maxing” referred to building up a character’s strengths in one particular area, to the point that its weaknesses no longer mattered.
According to Johnson, words like “looksmaxxing” gave the term its extra “x” and, ultimately, turned it into the trend it has become today. He said “maxxing” started standing out on its own, too, this year, in phrases like, “What are you maxxing?” or “Everyone’s maxxing something.”
“Looksmaxxing” remains the most popular version of the word by far. Johnson said its use rose more than 1,000% since the start of the year in the media that Dictionary.com analyzed, while “tokenmaxxing” also grew with the proliferation of AI tools.
What “maxxing” says about us
Johnson said the word captures a pressure many people feel, especially online, to constantly do, or be, more.
“Whether it’s at work and your career, whether it’s in school, in so many aspects of your life, just kind of being more is something that is a pressure that I think a lot of people can feel,” he said.
The pressure has also produced its own pushback, as playful versions of the word like “normalmaxxing” reject the drive to optimize everything while still using the same language.
“One of my favorite ‘maxxings’ is ‘nothingmaxxing,’ which is just completely paradoxical, right?” Johnson said. “It’s going all in an optimizing doing nothing, which also requires a lot of effort.”
The flexibility helps explain why the word spread so widely, he said, adding: “It resonates with people.”
2026 Word of the Year finalists
Dictionary.com pulled from different corners of internet culture, politics, technology and media to compile a list of finalists. Here are the others that were considered:
Affordability: the quality of being inexpensive, which is an issue at the center of American life and, now, the upcoming midterm elections, as people face increasing costs of housing, groceries, childcare and more.
Data center: a building or facility used for processing, storing or transmitting large amounts of computer data, which are cropping up more often around the U.S. with the rise of artificial intelligence.
Unc: short for “uncle,” Gen Z and Gen Alpha popularized this humorous and lightly pejorative slang term for an older person who’s uncool, trying too hard, or just doesn’t get it.
Odyssey: a long and eventful journey, such as that of Homer’s protagonist in his epic poem of the same name, which this summer was adapted into an ensemble blockbuster by director Christopher Nolan. (CBS News)
articles.summary: From AI chatbots to lifestyle trends, the concept of optimizing one’s life came sharply into focus in 2026. That’s why Dictionary.com picked “maxxing,” a reflection of our increasingly online society, as its latest Word of the Year.

articles.title: Sri Lanka to host World Buddhist Sangha Council’s 60th anniversary celebrations in November
articles.text:
Sri Lanka is set to host the 60th anniversary celebrations of the World Buddhist Sangha Council from November 28 to December 2, with the participation of Buddhist monks and delegates from around the world.
According to the President’s Media Division (PMD), the conference will commence on November 28 at the Nagananda International Institute for Buddhist Studies in Kelaniya, under the patronage of President Anura Kumara Dissanayake.
Several events are also scheduled to be held in Anuradhapura and Kandy as part of the celebrations.
A special discussion to review preparations for the international event was held at the Presidential Secretariat yesterday (26), with the participation of World Buddhist Sangha Council Organising Committee Chairman Ven. Dr. Bodagama Chandima Thera, Secretary-General Ven. Dr. Maitipe Wimalasara Maha Thera and Secretary to the President Dr. Nandika Sanath Kumanayake.
The meeting focused on arrangements for more than 600 delegates, including Buddhist monks representing countries across the world, approximately 250 Sri Lankans residing overseas and around 250 Sri Lankan Buddhist monks.
Special attention was given to ensuring security for foreign Buddhist monks and other delegates, alongside arrangements for medical services, first aid and essential infrastructure facilities.
Officials also discussed the potential economic benefits of the international gathering, noting that the arrival of a large number of foreign participants could contribute to foreign exchange earnings and promote Sri Lanka’s tourism industry.
Meanwhile, the World Buddhist Sangha Council has proposed providing Rs. 500,000 each to 15 Buddhist temples damaged by Cyclone Ditwah, to support their restoration.
The initiative, along with arrangements for infrastructure development and decorations at conference venues and surrounding cities, was also discussed.
The meeting was attended by senior Buddhist clergy, government officials and representatives of security agencies, including officials from the Ministry of Buddhasasana, Religious and Cultural Affairs, the Department of Buddhist Affairs, Sri Lanka Police and the Sri Lanka Army.

articles.title: Harry Kane and Alèxia Putellas win men’s and women’s Ballon d’Or awards
articles.text:
Harry Kane and Alèxia Putellas have been named the best men’s and women’s soccer players in the world at this year’s Ballon d’Or ceremony.
In a glitzy ceremony that was delayed by a rainy and traffic-logged night in London, the Beautiful Game’s great and good gathered to celebrate the very best players in the world.
After much debate, it was Kane who was named the men’s Ballon d’Or winner, beating Kylian Mbappé and Lamine Yamal to the prize.
The English striker enjoyed a simply brilliant season last year, scoring 73 goals in 65 competitive matches for club and country – winning the league and cup double with club Bayern Munich.
The 33-year-old was emotional during his speech, cheered onto the stage by chants of “Harry, Harry” from a home crowd.
“It being here in London as well has made it extra special,” Kane said after winning his first Ballon d’Or.
“Thank you very much. Thank you to everyone who voted for me. I can imagine it was really tough this year – some incredible players I was up against.”
Kane is the first Englishman to win the award since Michael Owen in 2001.
Meanwhile, Putellas won the women’s award for the third time. The 32-year-old was expected to beat her rivals after another dominant season with Barcelona Femení, where she was the heartbeat of the club’s unrivaled success.
She captained the side to a quadruple of trophies – the league title, two domestic cups and the Women’s Champions League – before signing for the London City Lionesses in England this summer.
“I don’t know what to say, too many things. Congrats to all the nominees, congrats to all the winners,” Putellas said in her acceptance speech on stage.
“That so many Barça players were nominated says a lot about the season we had. … It was my honor to be your captain.”
The voting for the men’s and women’s Ballon d’Or is down to selected journalists who vote on behalf of their nation.
Each voter ranks their 10 best players, with points distributed on a descending scale depending on their place in the list.
Spain and Barça dominate
The scene of hundreds of kids damaging security barriers and climbing buildings to get a better view of their heroes arriving on Monday was another reminder of how much this sport means to fans.
And many of the biggest names turned up to London’s historic Palladium Theatre, braving the wintry conditions on the red carpet.
Yamal drew one of the loudest reactions as he walked up the red carpet, and while he didn’t win the award he most wanted, the 19-year-old was named Young Talent of the Year for a third successive time.
It follows a trophy-laden season for both club and country in which the teenager won La Liga for Barcelona and the World Cup for Spain.
Meanwhile, Barça’s Vicky López was named the Women’s Young Talent of the Year for a second successive time, capping off a brilliant season with the Blaugrana that dominated across both the men’s and women’s categories.
The Spanish and Catalan dominance continued with Spain manager Luis de la Fuente claiming Men’s Coach of the Year after his World Cup glory and Barcelona Femení manager being named Women’s Coach of the Year after guiding his team to practically every trophy.
Full list of winners
Ballon d’Or: Harry Kane (Bayern Munich and England)
Ballon d’Or Fémenin: Alèxia Putellas (Barcelona Femení/London City Lionesses and Spain)
Men’s Club of the Year: Paris Saint-Germain
Women’s Club of the Year: Barcelona Femení
Men’s Young Talent of the Year: Lamine Yamal (Barcelona and Spain)
Women’s Young Talent of the Year: Vicky López (Barcelona Femení and Spain)
Men’s Coach of the Year: Luis de la Fuente (Spain)
Women’s Coach of the Year: Pere Romeu (Barcelona Femení)
Men’s Goalkeeper of the Year: Unai Simón (Athletic Bilbao and Spain)
Women’s Goalkeeper of the Year: Cata Coll (Barcelona Femení and Spain)
Sócrates Award (best humanitarian actions by a player): Bukayo Saka (Arsenal and England)
Men’s Striker of the Year: Harry Kane (Bayern Munich and England)
Women’s Striker of the Year: Charlyn Corral (CF Pachuca and Mexico) (CNN)
articles.summary: Harry Kane and Alèxia Putellas have been named the best men’s and women’s soccer players in the world at this year’s Ballon d’Or ceremony.

According to the Homagama Police, the suspect suddenly fell ill after being brought to the police station following his arrest. He was subsequently admitted to the Homagama Base Hospital for treatment, where he later died.
Following the incident, the Homagama Magistrate’s Court was informed, and the Acting Magistrate visited the Homagama Base Hospital to conduct a magisterial inquiry into the death.

articles.title: Cyclone Arnab intensifies: Warning issued to fishermen over rough seas and strong winds
articles.text:
The Department of Meteorology has issued a warning to naval and fishing communities against venturing into several sea areas in the Bay of Bengal, as Cyclonic Storm “Arnab” has intensified into a Very Severe Cyclonic Storm.
According to the department, the storm, which was located over the west-central Bay of Bengal, intensified further and was centred approximately 890 km northeast of Kankasanthurai at 2.30 a.m. today (27).
The cyclone is expected to move west-northwestwards until 5.30 p.m. today before changing direction towards the northwest and crossing the Andhra Pradesh coast in India as a Very Severe Cyclonic Storm by 11.30 a.m. tomorrow (28).
The department warned that wind speeds in the sea areas between latitudes 10°N and 20°N and longitudes 80°E and 95°E could increase to 80–140 kmph, accompanied by heavy thundershowers and waves reaching heights of 3–4 metres.
As a result, naval and fishing communities have been advised not to venture into these sea areas until further notice, while those already operating in the affected regions have been urged to move away immediately.
Meanwhile, showers or thundershowers are expected at several places in the sea areas surrounding Sri Lanka, with southwesterly winds ranging between 30 and 40 kmph.
Wind speeds could increase to 60–65 kmph at times in the deep and shallow sea areas extending from Colombo to Mullaitivu via Galle, Matara, Hambantota, Pottuvil and Batticaloa.
Other sea areas around the island could experience wind speeds of up to 50 kmph.
The department further warned that sea conditions along the Colombo–Mullaitivu coastal stretch could become very rough at times, while other sea areas may also experience rough conditions.
Wave heights could increase to 2–2.5 metres in the sea areas off the coast extending from Puttalam to Pottuvil via Colombo, Galle and Matara.
Additionally, temporarily strong gusty winds of 60–70 kmph and very rough seas are expected during thundershowers.
The Department of Meteorology has urged naval and fishing communities to remain vigilant and closely monitor future weather forecasts and advisories.

articles.title: CMC explains delays in Baseline Road construction work
articles.text:
The Colombo Municipal Council (CMC) has clarified the reasons for the ongoing construction work along Baseline Road, attributing delays to difficulties in identifying existing underground utility networks.
Colombo Mayor Vraîe Cally Balthazaar said the construction is part of two major underground sewerage development projects in Kirulapone and Kirula–Narahenpita, being implemented under the Greater Colombo Water and Wastewater Management Improvement Investment Programme at a combined investment of approximately Rs. 25 billion.
According to the Mayor, the Kirulapone project, valued at approximately Rs. 14.5 billion, is funded by the Government of Sri Lanka, while the Kirula–Narahenpita project, valued at approximately Rs. 10 billion, is supported by the European Investment Bank.
The projects aim to establish underground sewerage networks to collect wastewater from residential properties and transport it through pipelines to pumping stations for proper management and safe disposal.
Explaining the delays along Baseline Road, the Mayor said one of the main challenges has been locating existing underground infrastructure, including electricity cables, water supply pipelines, telecommunications cables and stormwater drainage systems.
She said the CMC has been coordinating with the Ceylon Electricity Board (CEB), National Water Supply and Drainage Board (NWSDB), Sri Lanka Telecom (SLT), Dialog and other service providers to identify these utilities.
However, despite employing various technical methods, locating certain underground services has proven difficult, slowing construction activities.
The Mayor explained that excavation cannot proceed without accurately identifying these utilities, as accidental damage could disrupt essential services and pose serious safety risks.
The CMC aims to complete the pipeline construction work along Baseline Road by December 2026, although the broader sewerage development projects will continue beyond that date.
The Mayor further revealed that the Kirulapone project, which commenced in 2017, was suspended in 2022 due to the economic crisis. Construction resumed in October 2025 after funding and payment-related issues were resolved under the current government.
Meanwhile, 26 households in the project areas, including those near the Kalinga Mawatha sewerage pumping station, have been temporarily relocated as a safety precaution.
The affected families have been provided rental assistance to secure alternative accommodation and will be permitted to return once the relevant construction work is completed.
The Mayor also assured that sections of Thalakotuwa Gardens Road damaged during construction would be restored upon completion of the necessary work.
She added that the projects are being implemented in collaboration with the Ministry of Public Administration, Provincial Councils and Local Government, while supervision is being carried out directly by CMC staff without a separate external supervision institution.
The Kirulapone sewerage project is expected to be completed by December 2027, while the Kirula–Narahenpita project is scheduled for completion by August 2028.
Acknowledging the inconvenience caused by road excavations and traffic disruptions, the Mayor thanked residents and motorists for their patience, emphasising that the projects are essential to improving Colombo’s long-term wastewater management infrastructure.
articles.summary: The Colombo Municipal Council (CMC) has clarified the reasons for the ongoing construction work along Baseline Road, attributing delays to difficulties in identifying existing underground utility networks. The CMC aims to complete the pipeline construction work along Baseline Road by December 2026, although the broader sewerage development projects will continue beyond that date.

articles.title: UN inquiry finds Israel committed war crimes and crimes against humanity in Palestine
articles.text:
The United Nations Independent International Commission of Inquiry has concluded that Israel has committed war crimes and crimes against humanity, including extermination, persecution, torture, rape and other forms of sexual violence, against Palestinians in the Occupied Palestinian Territory.
In a statement shared on social media, United Nations Geneva highlighted the Commission’s findings, stating that Israeli forces had intentionally targeted Palestinian civilians.
The findings are detailed in the Commission’s fifth report to the UN General Assembly, dated October 14, 2026, which examines killings and serious bodily and mental harm caused by Israeli and Palestinian security forces since October 2023.
According to the report, more than 75,000 Palestinians have been killed across the Occupied Palestinian Territory since October 7, 2023, including at least 21,500 children and 11,000 women.
The Commission concluded that Israeli military operations in the West Bank formed part of a widespread and systematic attack against Palestinian civilians, involving deliberate killings, excessive use of force and discriminatory practices.
It further found that Israeli authorities and security forces had committed crimes against humanity, including extermination, torture, rape, sexual violence and persecution based on nationality, race and ethnicity.
The report also found that Palestinian children had been deliberately targeted, with the Commission concluding that Israeli forces had committed age-based persecution against children in both Gaza and the West Bank.
Regarding Gaza, the Commission reaffirmed its earlier findings that Israeli authorities and forces had committed war crimes, crimes against humanity and genocide. It concluded that incidents investigated in its latest report demonstrated the continuation of acts committed with genocidal intent.
The Commission also documented additional cases of sexual violence against Palestinian detainees, including rape, forced nudity and other forms of degrading treatment.
The report further noted that Israeli airstrikes in the West Bank had resulted in 254 Palestinian deaths between October 7, 2023, and September 30, 2026, compared to six deaths from airstrikes between 2008 and October 6, 2023.
The Commission called for an end to Israel’s unlawful occupation of Palestinian territory and measures to ensure accountability for violations of international law.
Israel has rejected the Commission’s findings, describing the report as part of a misinformation campaign aimed at demonising the country.

articles.summary: The United Nations Independent International Commission of Inquiry has concluded that Israel has committed war crimes and crimes against humanity, including extermination, persecution, torture, rape and other forms of sexual violence, against Palestinians in the Occupied Palestinian Territory. articles.title: Anthropic warns of ‘catastrophic risk’ to humankind ahead of blockbuster share listing
articles.text:
Anthropic has warned that artificial intelligence could pose catastrophic or existential risks to humanity as it unveiled details of its planned blockbuster stock market listing in the United States.
The firm’s valuation is expected to surpass that of SpaceX, which set the record as the largest-ever stock listing at an initial valuation of approximately $1.8 trillion during the summer. While Anthropic has disclosed that it will list on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol ANT, making it the first pure-play AI company to go public, it has not yet revealed the number of shares to be offered, their price range, or the exact date for the listing. In financial details filed on Monday, the Claude chatbot developer reported a first-half loss exceeding $80.7 billion against $16.3 billion in revenue, while maintaining $112.4 billion in cash or equivalents.
In its regulatory filing ahead of the debut, Anthropic acknowledged widespread concerns raised by policymakers, regulators, researchers, and internal staff regarding the safety of advanced AI models. The company stated that if advanced AI systems are not developed, deployed, and operated with appropriate safeguards, oversight, and security, they could pose catastrophic or existential risks, particularly if misused, replicated, weaponized, or granted high autonomy.
Founded five years ago by Chief Executive Officer Dario Amodei, his sister Daniela Amodei, and five co-founders, Anthropic first announced its intention to go public in June, prompting key rival OpenAI to announce its own plans for a public listing early next year. Following these announcements, both companies faced a series of cybersecurity and technological breaches involving autonomous AI agents, alongside public warnings from current and former employees about inadequate safeguards for future harms. Adding to its challenges, the owners of Elvis Presley’s music rights filed a lawsuit against Anthropic on Monday, alleging that hundreds of the star’s songs were used without authorization to train its Claude models.

articles.title: 16 locations record over 100mm of rainfall as severe weather hits Sri Lanka
articles.text:
Torrential weather conditions across Sri Lanka have triggered exceptional rainfall figures in southwestern catchments and hill slopes, with multiple stations recording well over 100 mm of rain during a 24-hour period ending at 6PM on October 26, 2026, according to joint data released by the National Building Research Organisation (NBRO) and the Department of Meteorology.
Leading the nationwide rainfall tally, Samanalagama in the Dewalegama Grama Niladhari Division within Pelmadulla Divisional Secretariat of Ratnapura District recorded a peak total of 185.4 mm. Heavy downpours also drenched surrounding catchments across Ratnapura and Kalutara districts, including Gavaragiriya with 170.4 mm, Pahiyangala in Bulathsinhala with 170.2 mm, Opanayake with 164.4 mm, and Palabaddala with 163.8 mm.
In total, 16 individual monitoring locations across Ratnapura, Kalutara, Nuwara Eliya, and Kegalle districts surpassed the 100 mm rainfall threshold within 24 hours. High-volume measurements include Noragolla at 157.2 mm, Namunuthantenna in Ayagama at 152.6 mm, Palawela in Elapatha at 152.2 mm, Delmella in Bulathsinhala at 150.6 mm, Ratnapura town at 149.6 mm, Galaboda at 141.4 mm, Kiribathgala at 134 mm, Wewelvatta at 131 mm, Kukule at 127 mm, and Kalawana at 123.4 mm. Upcountry catchments in Nuwara Eliya and Kegalle also recorded heavy downpours, with Norton receiving 114 mm, Watawala recording 108 mm, and Galapitamada logging 104.2 mm.
Disaster management authorities warn that sustained precipitation of this volume on heavily saturated terrain significantly increases the immediate risk of localized flash flooding along main river valleys and sudden slope failures in landslide-prone mountain areas. Residents living in designated high-risk hazard zones across Ratnapura, Kalutara, Kegalle and Nuwara Eliya districts are advised to remain alert and closely follow safety advisories issued by regional disaster response officers.

articles.title: Severe weather leaves one dead and over 10,000 affected across 12 districts
articles.text:
Heavy rainfall and adverse weather conditions sweeping across Sri Lanka have left one person dead, one injured, affected over 10,000 residents, disrupted transport and power infrastructure nationwide, according to the official Situation Summary Report released by the Disaster Management Centre (DMC) at 6PM on October 26, 2026.
A total of 10,545 individuals from 2,736 families across 12 districts and 57 Divisional Secretariat divisions have been impacted by the severe weather. One person died due to drowning in Madampe, Puttalam district, while one individual was injured in Ingiriya, Kalutara district, after a tree fell onto a home. To assist affected residents, emergency authorities have established four safety centers across Colombo, Ratnapura and Mannar accommodating 182 people from 67 families, while 60 individuals are staying with relatives as two homes were fully destroyed and 215 suffered partial damage.
The heavy downpours have caused significant disruptions to the island’s transport services. Sri Lanka Railways has suspended train operations on the Main Line between Gampola and Nanu Oya, running services only between Nanu Oya and Badulla. Train services between Peradeniya and Matale have also been completely halted. Additionally, key road stretches in Kalutara, including the Bulathsinhala–Molkawa road and the Galathara–Pareigama road, have been inundated under up to 2.5 feet of water, blocking traffic.
The deluge follows rainfall exceeding 180 mm in regions such as Samanala Wewa (185.4 mm), Gavaragiriya (170.4 mm), and Pahiyangala (170.2 mm) over the past 24 hours. Rising water levels have forced engineers to open spill gates at major reservoirs including Rajanganaya (18 gates), Deduru Oya (8 gates), Tabowa (4 gates), Angamuwa (2 gates), Kala Wewa (2 gates), and Kukule Ganga (2 gates discharging 148m3/s). Major hydro dams including Norton, Canyon, Laxapana, and Polpitiya are also actively spilling. According to the Department of Meteorology, Deep Depression ‘Onab’ over the Bay of Bengal is expected to intensify into a severe cyclonic storm, continuing to draw strong cross-island wind currents and localized heavy rains above 75 mm across multiple provinces.
In response, the National Building Research Organisation (NBRO) has placed several high-risk divisions across Ratnapura, Kalutara, Kandy, Kegalle, Nuwara Eliya, and Kurunegala under Level 2 Amber and Level 3 Red landslide evacuation warnings. Meanwhile, tri-forces personnel, Sri Lanka Police, Coast Guard, and Civil Security Department units equipped with rescue boats and search teams have been deployed islandwide, with Air Force helicopters stationed across key airbases on standby for emergency airlifts.
articles.summary: Heavy rainfall and adverse weather conditions sweeping across Sri Lanka have left one person dead, one injured, affected over 10,000 residents, disrupted transport and power infrastructure nationwide, according to the official Situation Summary Report released by the Disaster Management Centre (DMC) at 6PM on October 26, 2026.

In a post on X marking Abhidhamma Day, the Indian minister highlighted the message delivered by the monk, who represents the Sihanada International Meditation Community in Sri Lanka.
Ven. Seeladassana delivered the message following an invitation from the International Buddhist Confederation (IBC), praising India’s initiatives to strengthen the global Buddhist community through spiritual diplomacy, the sharing of sacred relics and the preservation of Buddhist heritage.
Addressing Prime Minister Modi, the monk said India’s efforts had provided Buddhists worldwide with opportunities to pay homage to sacred relics and visit important pilgrimage destinations, including Sarnath, Bodh Gaya and Kushinagar.
He also welcomed India’s decision to recognise Pali as a classical language, describing it as a significant step towards preserving the original teachings of the Buddha.
The monk emphasised that preserving Buddhism should extend beyond historical sites and sacred relics to include the practice and theoretical understanding of the Dhamma.
Referring to the historical Buddhist relationship between Sri Lanka and India, Ven. Seeladassana recalled the arrival of Arahant Mahinda in Sri Lanka and the close ties between Emperor Ashoka and King Devanampiyatissa.
He called for stronger cooperation between the International Buddhist Confederation, the governments of India and Sri Lanka, and the Buddhist clergy to safeguard Buddhist teachings for future generations.
In his post, Shekhawat expressed gratitude to Prime Minister Modi for his leadership and referred to the government’s efforts to foster mutual respect, cultural understanding and stronger spiritual ties with Buddhist communities internationally.
He also highlighted the historical and spiritual bonds between India and Sri Lanka, describing the two countries as united by their shared Buddhist heritage.
The minister referred to Modi’s motto, “Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas,” saying it continued to inspire India’s engagement with the global Buddhist community.

articles.title: Sri Lanka’s exports to India rise 12.3%, India remains second-largest export market
articles.text:
India has overtaken the United Kingdom to become Sri Lanka’s second-largest export destination, with exports to India recording a 12.3% year-on-year increase during the first nine months of 2026, according to the Sri Lanka Export Development Board (EDB).
Exports to India reached US$ 889.84 million between January and September 2026, strengthening its position as Sri Lanka’s second-largest export market after the United States.
In September alone, Sri Lanka’s exports to India increased by 29.65% compared with the corresponding month in 2025, reaching US$ 113.22 million.
Meanwhile, exports to the United Kingdom declined by 9.33% during the first nine months of 2026 to US$ 654.36 million. September exports to the UK also fell by 3.17% to US$ 71.71 million.
The United States remained Sri Lanka’s largest single export destination, with cumulative exports reaching US$ 2.25 billion during January–September 2026, a marginal increase of 0.05% year-on-year.
According to the EDB, Sri Lanka’s total exports reached US$ 13.61 billion during the first nine months of 2026, recording a 5.04% increase compared with US$ 12.96 billion during the corresponding period in 2025.
Merchandise exports increased by 5.35% to US$ 10.76 billion, while services exports grew by 3.88% to US$ 2.85 billion.
The EDB said the growth across several key international markets highlighted the importance of expanding Sri Lanka’s export destinations and strengthening competitiveness in global trade.

The Irrigation Department has reported minor flood levels at three monitoring stations in the Kalu Ganga basin, while several other rivers across Sri Lanka have reached alert levels following heavy rainfall.

At Ratnapura, the Kalu Ganga reached 8.20 metres, exceeding the minor flood level of 7.50 metres. The river at Kalawellawa (Millakanda) reached 6.50 metres, meeting its minor flood threshold.
Meanwhile, the Maguru Ganga at Magura rose to 4.69 metres, above the alert level of 4.00 metres.
In the Kelani Ganga basin, water levels at Glencourse reached 15.12 metres and were rising, exceeding the alert level of 15.00 metres.
Alert levels were also reported at Holombuwa along Gurugoda Oya and Norwood along Kehelgamu Oya, although water levels at both locations were falling.
The Gin Ganga at Thawalama reached 4.10 metres, exceeding its alert level of 4.00 metres, with water levels continuing to rise.

Meanwhile, the Mahaweli Ganga at Peradeniya remained at alert level, although its water level had begun to fall.

articles.title: ‘We are not slaves of the SJB’: Rishad Bathiudeen criticises Sajith’s political direction
articles.text:
Former Minister and All Ceylon Makkal Congress (ACMC) leader Rishad Bathiudeen has expressed disappointment over the recent political direction of the Samagi Jana Balawegaya (SJB), warning Opposition Leader Sajith Premadasa against abandoning the principles on which their political alliance was built.
“We are not slaves of the SJB. The SJB is a political party, and we are partners in that alliance,” Bathiudeen said.
He said his party had worked tirelessly to support Premadasa during two presidential elections, with supporters spending millions of rupees and campaigning day and night.
“We brought together the votes of our people and contributed them to the alliance. It was based on agreements between our parties that National List appointments, parliamentary positions and ministerial portfolios were allocated,” he said.
Bathiudeen expressed concern that the SJB appeared to be moving away from the political positions it maintained during the presidential election.
“I am saddened by their current approach. It appears to me that they are moving away from the position they held during the presidential election,” he said.
The former minister revealed that he had personally contacted Premadasa by telephone to convey his concerns.
“I told him that we stood with him because of his policies and principles. Even if there are political setbacks, he should not compromise those principles,” Bathiudeen said.
Referring to President Anura Kumara Dissanayake and the National People’s Power (NPP), Bathiudeen said the ruling party’s electoral success demonstrated the importance of public confidence in political principles.
He said voters had supported the NPP because they believed in its stated opposition to racism and religious extremism, as well as its promise of systemic change.
Bathiudeen said he remained dissatisfied with the SJB’s recent conduct.
He warned that Sri Lanka’s past experiences demonstrated the dangers of ethnic and religious extremism.
“Our country’s history has shown us that racism and religious extremism are not good for the country, its communities or future generations,” he said.
Bathiudeen’s ACMC formally backed Premadasa’s presidential candidacy in August 2024, signing an agreement with the SJB-led alliance.

articles.text:
The Department of Irrigation has issued Amber flood warnings for low-lying areas in the Kelani River and Attanagalu Oya basins through 6PM tomorrow (October 27), following heavy rainfall and the opening of spill gates at the Basnagoda Reservoir.

articles.title: 29-year-old dies in police custody: 3 Homagama Police officers interdicted
articles.text:
Three police officers attached to the Homagama Police Station, including the Officer-in-Charge (OIC) of the Crimes Division and two sub-inspectors, have been interdicted over alleged administrative lapses following the death of a suspect in police custody.
The action follows the death of 29-year-old Ishara Harsha Kumara, a resident of Kiriwaththuduwa, who died after being taken into police custody in connection with a drug-related investigation on October 25.
The suspect’s family has alleged that he was severely assaulted by police officers while being held at the Homagama Police Station.
According to relatives, Kumara was unable to walk after being taken for questioning and had to be carried by several officers. They also alleged that he had visible injuries and was bleeding when he was returned to the police cell.
Family members claimed that police arranged for him to be taken to Homagama Base Hospital only after repeated requests for medical assistance, and that he was already dead when he arrived.
However, police have maintained that the suspect suddenly fell ill while in custody and died after being admitted to hospital.
The Homagama Magistrate’s Court ordered a post-mortem examination to determine the cause of death, while a preliminary investigation was initiated under the supervision of the Homagama Assistant Superintendent of Police.
Meanwhile, Public Security Minister Ananda Wijepala has instructed Inspector General of Police Priyantha Weerasuriya to conduct a prompt and independent investigation into the incident.
The minister has also directed that appropriate legal action be taken based on the post-mortem findings and the outcome of the investigation.
articles.summary: Three police officers attached to the Homagama Police Station, including the Officer-in-Charge (OIC) of the Crimes Division and two sub-inspectors, have been interdicted over alleged administrative lapses following the death of a suspect in police custody.
